description: This dataset provides sediment geochemical measurements from a single sampling event (LTp22-1) at a fixed location in Mexico (21.277661°N, 104.690167°W) at an elevation of 1430 meters, collected on April 8, 2022. It includes depth-resolved data (0-0.185 meters) with corresponding ages ranging from 1885.5 to 2018.8 years, allowing for temporal analysis of sediment layers. The dataset contains concentrations of 19 chemical elements (Si, K, Ca, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Ni, Cu, Zn, Ge, Sr, Zr, Cd, Ce, Ta) measured in closed-loop recirculation (CLR) format, along with a coherence scattering metric (icoh/coh scat). Semantically, the data represents geological measurements with temporal (age) and spatial (latitude/longitude) references, enabling studies of sediment composition over time. This dataset is valuable for research in sediment geochemistry, paleoenvironmental reconstruction, and environmental monitoring, particularly for analyzing elemental trends and their potential links to historical or anthropogenic influences.
